Jātūkarṇya
------------------------------------------
The dharmaśāstra literature is very vast. Many writers quote the earlier writers as authorities to support their own views. One such ancient author is जातूकर्ण्य (also spelt as Jātūkarṇi or Jātūkarṇa). He perhaps lived earlier than the 3rd century A. D.
Jātūkarṇya has been quoted (in verses as also in prose) by विश्वरूप (9th century A. D.), in the Mitākṣarā of विज्ञानेश्वर (12th century A. D.), हरदत्त (circa A. D. 1100-1300), अपरार्क (12th century A. D.) and others.
Some of the views attributed to him are: a pupil should not suddenly put questions to his teacher in an assembly; prohibition of marrying another wife of a lower caste when already having one wife of one’s own caste; प्रायश्चित्त for a boy before उपनयन, for accidentally drinking liquor and so on.
His work (not available now) was probably in the form of sūtras and must have dealt with subjects like आचार (conduct), śrāddha (obsequial rites), some sacrifices and some aspects of अस्त्रोलोग्य्.

jātakarma
(‘birth-ceremonies’)
------------------------------------------
The Hindu smṛtis and the धर्म-śāstras prescribe sixteen सṁस्कारस् or purificatory sacraments—generally termed ‘ṣodaśa-सṁस्कारस्’—for every human being. Out of them hardly five or six have survived to this day. And, जातकर्म (which seems to be very ancient) is one of them, though comparatively much less in vogue.
This saṁskāra has to be performed by the ड़थेर् of the baby, just born and before the umbilical cord is cut.
The several steps in it are: medhā-जनन (inducing medhas or intelligence by making the baby lick ghee or honey uttering the vyāhṛtis—bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ and suvaḥ); आयुष्य (the rite of ensuring a long life by muttering some mantras in the right ear of the baby); honouring the earth where the baby was delivered and reciting some more mantras to induce adamantine strength in the baby.
Later, the naval cord is severed, the baby washed and given to the मोथेर् for breast-feeding.
Some authorities add the performance of a होम and giving a secret name to the baby also.
See also ṢOḌAŚASAṀSKĀRAS.

jāti
(‘that which comes by birth’)
------------------------------------------
In the Indian philosophical systems, categorisation of things is an important item of discussion. One such is ‘sāmānya’ or ‘jāti’. It indicates the common quality of a number of things which are similar in certain respects.
For instance, in a number of cows, which may appear to be different in size, colour or other features, there is a common quality, which can be called ‘gotva-जाति’ or ‘cowness’ which comes to them by birth (= जाति).
In the न्याय system of philosophy the word ‘jāti’ is used in the technical sense of ‘futility’ (vide Nyāyasūtras 1.2.18). It means an unfair reply based on a false analogy. It consists of basing a futile argument on any kind of similarity or dissimilarity between two things to controvert another sound argument.
For instance: If one argues, ‘Sound is non-eternal, because it is an effect like a pot,’ and another person objects to it saying that sound must be eternal, because it is incorporeal like the sky, this objection is a kind of जाति since there is no universal relation between the incorporeal and the eternal.
As for जाति or caste, see CASTE SYSTEM.

jātijñāna
(‘knowledge of [previous] births’)
------------------------------------------
A योगि develops extraordinary powers by ‘saṁyama’ or समाधि (perfect concentration) preceded by धारणा (fixing the मिन्द् on an object) and ध्यान (continuous meditation). If he practises सṁयम on his own सṁस्कारस् or residual potencies of his मिन्द्, he will get a direct knowledge of his previous births or lives (jāti = birth, ज्ञान = knowledge) because these सṁस्कारस् have been caused by the experiences in those lives (vide Yogasūtras of पतञ्जलि 3.18).

jātaka
(‘[map of celestial objects] at the time of birth’)
------------------------------------------
That the स्तर्स् and the प्लनेत्स् in the universe have a bearing on the lives of human beings and affect them is an ancient belief existing in all the cultures of the world. The science that has evolved and developed this belief is known as अस्त्रोलोग्य्. In हिन्दुइस्म् it is called ‘Jyautiṣa or Jyotiśśāstra’.
The जातक or the होरोस्चोपे (also called ‘kuṇḍali’) which gives the position of the various प्लनेत्स् and the स्तर्स् at the actual time of birth of a human being, is the basic diagram for all astrological calculations.
Fixing the position of the प्लनेत्स् at the time of birth and drawing the होरोस्चोपे is an intricate process. It can be done only by expert astrologers with the aid of almanacs accurately prepared by competent persons.
See also JYAUTIṢA.
